KIPLMC/Geometry.lean.title: The actual scaled particle force and its geometry
KIPLMC/Geometry.lean.summary: The shared IPLA state stores \(z=(\theta,X^1/\sqrt N,\ldots,X^N/\sqrt N)\) in a Euclidean coordinate space with independent parameter and latent dimensions. This module keeps physical time, scaling velocities by the same spatial map. In this convention the kinetic temperature is \(1/N\), the potential is the particle average \(\bar U_N\), and the force is its actual gradient. It is equivalent to the manuscript's additional time change but avoids reimplementing the shared kinetic step.

steps.title: Define the average and prove that its gradient is the force
steps.body: State reuses the scaled Euclidean IPLA state. The existing lifted potential is \(V_N(z)=\sum_iU(\theta,\sqrt Nz_i)\). Define \(\bar U_N=V_N/N\) and \(F=\nabla V_N/N\). To prove \(\nabla\bar U_N=F\), compare their inner products against an arbitrary vector. The derivative rule for a scalar multiple gives \(D\bar U_N[w]=N^{-1}DV_N[w]\), and the inner-product characterization of gradients identifies the two vectors. Lean uses ext_inner_right, the proved differentiability of the lifted potential, and HasFDerivAt.const_mul. For \(N>0\), cancellation of the nonzero particle number gives \(V_N=N\bar U_N\).

steps.title: Average the lifted strong convexity
steps.body: The existing particle geometry proves \(V_N\) is \(Nm\)-strongly convex whenever the pair potential is \(m\)-strongly convex. Multiply its convex-combination inequality by \(N^{-1}>0\): the function terms become \(\bar U_N\), and the quadratic correction \(N^{-1}(Nm)\|x-y\|^2/2\) becomes \(m\|x-y\|^2/2\). Lean constructs the strong-convexity structure directly, obtains the lifted inequality, multiplies it by the nonnegative inverse particle number, and uses field_simp and ring to cancel constants. The proof requires positive particle count but imposes no artificial equality of the parameter and latent dimensions.

steps.title: Recover the mean parameter force and unaveraged latent force
steps.body: The parameter block of \( abla V_N\) is the sum of pair parameter gradients, so \(F_ heta=N^{-1}\sum_i abla_ heta U( heta,X^i)\). Each latent block of \( abla V_N\) is \(\sqrt N abla_xU\). Dividing by \(N\) and undoing the spatial scaling gives \(\sqrt N F_i= abla_xU( heta,X^i)\). The parameter proof simplifies with the existing gradient-coordinate theorem. The latent proof expands coordinate scalar multiplication, groups the coefficient into \((\sqrt N)^2N^{-1}\), rewrites \((\sqrt N)^2=N\), and cancels the nonzero \(N\). These identities verify the actual force used by both particle algorithms.

steps.title: The force retains the pair smoothness constant
steps.body: The shared lifted gradient has Lipschitz constant \(NL\). Since \(F=\nabla V_N/N\), its difference satisfies \(\|F(x)-F(y)\|\le N^{-1}(NL)\|x-y\|=L\|x-y\|\). Lean starts from the existing lifted Lipschitz estimate, rewrites norms of scalar multiples with the nonnegative inverse particle count, multiplies the inequality by that inverse, and cancels \(N\). This proves that the physical-time scaled force has a smoothness constant independent of the number of particles, a key feature of the favorable KIPLMC1 scaling.

KIPLMC/Exponential.lean.title: KIPLMC1 reuses the shared exponential integrator
KIPLMC/Exponential.lean.summary: There is one exponential-step implementation: KineticLangevin.exponentialStep. KIPLMC1 supplies the proved averaged particle force and the common scaled-coordinate thermal amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\). The coordinate identities recover the paper's Algorithm 1 directly, including its separate velocity and position innovations. Noise covariance and independent-Gaussian law conditions must still be established for any stochastic convergence theorem.

steps.title: Supply the particle temperature to the shared map
steps.body: kineticAmplitude is \(a_N=\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\). kiplmc1Step calls the shared exponential map with force \(F\) and additive phase innovation \(a_N\,\text{noise}\). Consequently every block uses exactly the same friction response functions. In physical time and scaled coordinates this is an inverse temperature \(N\) kinetic system. The definition accepts arbitrary innovations; when used as the algorithm their velocity–position pair must have the common Gram covariance from the kinetic library.

steps.title: Recover both parameter updates
steps.body:
Parameter coordinates are unchanged by spatial rescaling. Substitute \(F_ heta=N^{-1}\sum_i abla_ heta U_i\) in the two shared expressions:

\[V^{ heta+}=\psi_0V^ heta- rac{\psi_1}N\sum_i abla_ heta U_i+a_N\xi_ heta,\quad heta^+= heta+\psi_1V^ heta- rac{\psi_2}N\sum_i abla_ heta U_i+a_N\xi'_ heta.\]

The proofs unfold the shared map, evaluate scalar multiplication in Euclidean coordinates, rewrite the proved force identity, and normalize division as multiplication by an inverse. The distinct projections of noise retain the correlated but generally unequal velocity and position increments.

steps.title: Undo the latent temperature and force scaling
steps.body: For \(N>0\), \(\sqrt N\sqrt{2\gamma/N}=\sqrt{2\gamma}\). Lean combines square roots using nonnegativity of \(N\), then cancels the positive particle number inside the root. Multiply each latent coordinate of the shared step by \(\sqrt N\). The force identity gives \(\sqrt NF_i=\nabla_xU_i\); the amplitude identity restores \(\sqrt{2\gamma}\) noise. Thus the physical latent velocity and position updates have the unaveraged pair force and the paper's latent thermal scale. The two coordinate proofs distribute multiplication, rewrite these exact identities and finish scalar rearrangement with ring.

steps.title: Construct the numerical recursion from a supplied innovation stream
steps.body: kiplmc1Chain starts from the given phase and uses innovation number \(n\) in the successor update. Each step is the shared exponential map specialized to the actual particle force. Recursive construction proves there is an explicit sequence for every prescribed stream; it is not an assumed sequence satisfying a desired estimate. To obtain the paper's actual random chain, one must additionally equip this stream with independent centered Gaussian pairs of the right covariance and prove its independence from initialization, measurability and finite moments.

KIPLMC/Splitting.lean.title: KIPLMC2 is exactly the shared OBABO composition
KIPLMC/Splitting.lean.summary: In scaled physical-time particle coordinates every velocity block has temperature \(1/N\). The parameter coordinates stay unchanged. Multiplying a latent coordinate by \(\sqrt N\) recovers the physical latent position and velocity and the unit-temperature latent noise used in Algorithm 2. The module proves these coordinate identities for the actual five-subflow map; no OBABO contraction theorem is hidden in the definitions.

steps.title: Define the scaled thermostat and half velocity
steps.body: Let \(\delta=e^{-\gamma h/2}\) and \(\sigma_N=\sqrt{(1-\delta^2)/N}\). thermalAmplitude defines \(\sigma_N\), kiplmc2Step passes it and the actual force \(F\) to the shared OBABO map, and halfVelocity records \(v_{1/2}=\delta v+\sigma_N\xi-hF(x)/2\). The algorithm uses this newly formed half velocity for its full position drift. The second force kick is evaluated at the new position, and the final OU half step receives the distinct noise \(\xi'\). Both the position and velocity projection formulas are definitional equalities, proved by rfl.

steps.title: The parameter half velocity contains the average gradient
steps.body:
Evaluating the half velocity on parameter index \(j\) gives

\[(v_{1/2})_{\theta,j}=\delta v_{\theta,j}+\sigma_N\xi_{\theta,j} -\frac{h}{2N}\sum_i\nabla_\theta U(\theta,X^i)_j.\]

Lean unfolds the half-velocity definition, distributes coordinate evaluation over vector addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication, then substitutes force_parameter. The remaining equality is scalar rational algebra, discharged by ring. This proof keeps the particle mean in the actual force rather than adding an assumed algorithm-equivalence premise.

steps.title: Undo latent scaling in the first O and B substeps
steps.body:
The thermostat identity is \(\sqrt N\sigma_N=\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\). Its proof combines square roots and cancels the positive \(N\) inside the argument. Multiplying the latent half velocity by \(\sqrt N\) then gives

\[\sqrt N(v_{1/2})_i=\delta(\sqrt Nv_i)+\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\xi_i-\frac h2\nabla_xU(\theta,X^i).\]

The coordinate proof expands multiplication through the three terms, applies the proved thermostat and force-unscaling identities, and normalizes multiplication order with ring. This yields exactly the physical latent OU refresh and unaveraged force kick.

steps.title: Recover physical parameter and latent position drifts
steps.body: The common position formula is \(z^+=z+h v_{1/2}\). Its parameter coordinate reads \(\theta^+=\theta+hV^\theta_{1/2}\) directly because that coordinate was not scaled; its theorem is definitional. In a latent coordinate, multiply both sides by \(\sqrt N\) and distribute: \(X^{i+}=X^i+hV^{x_i}_{1/2}\). Lean rewrites the shared position identity, simplifies Euclidean coordinate operations and closes the scalar distributive equality with ring. Together with the half-velocity and final-velocity identities, these are the paper's complete pointwise OBABO stages. Gaussian transition laws and their numerical bias remain separate analytic assertions.

KIPLMC/Target.lean.title: The normalized kinetic Gibbs candidate and sharp parameter concentration
KIPLMC/Target.lean.summary: The velocity-first phase target is the product of an explicit Gaussian thermal velocity measure and the already normalized lifted Gibbs position measure. Its parameter marginal is the powered likelihood, and its concentration radius has the paper's sharp dimension coefficient. These results concern a concrete probability measure; the module deliberately does not claim invariance of that measure under a kinetic diffusion.

steps.title: Construct thermal velocities as a Gaussian pushforward
steps.body: Start with the standard Gaussian on the scaled particle Euclidean space and map \(v\mapsto v/\sqrt N\). velocityTarget defines this measure, giving covariance \(I/N\) for positive \(N\). The probability proof uses measurability of the scalar map, evaluates its preimage of the whole space, and obtains mass one. The definition also makes sense at \(N=0\) under Lean's total inverse convention, but the physical target and subsequent normalization theorems require \(N>0\). No unspecified Gaussian velocity law is assumed.

steps.title: Normalize the product and compute its position marginal
steps.body: gibbsPhaseTarget is \(\mathcal N(0,I/N)\otimes\pi_N\), with velocity first. Joint strong convexity and differentiability of the original pair potential imply that the shared lifted Gibbs target \(\pi_N\) is a probability measure. Lean installs that proved instance and infers probability of the product. Mapping the product by its second projection integrates out the first factor, whose total mass is one, so the result is exactly \(\pi_N\). The proof uses Measure.map_snd_prod and simplifies the mass scalar. This computes the normalized marginal rather than merely comparing unnormalized density expressions.

steps.title: Identify the actual powered likelihood parameter marginal
steps.body: Map the phase target to \(\theta\) by composing position projection with the parameter continuous linear map. The pushforward composition theorem identifies this with first taking the position marginal and then the parameter marginal. The preceding result gives the exact lifted Gibbs position law; the shared IPLA theorem identifies its parameter marginal as \(p_\theta(y)^N\) after normalization. Measurability of both maps is provided explicitly. The theorem therefore connects the concrete phase target with the same normalized marginal target used by the concentration proof.

steps.title: Construct the unique marginal maximizer and its sharp second moment
steps.body: Joint strong convexity makes the negative log marginal strongly convex after latent integration. The shared IPLA theorem supplies existence and uniqueness of its minimizer, equivalently of the marginal likelihood maximizer. For that \(\theta_*\), the checked sharp concentration theorem gives \(\int\|\theta-\theta_*\|^2d\pi_\Theta\le d_\theta/(Nm)\). The declarations reuse these proved theorems for the actual target, not an abstract measure with a stated concentration field. The last theorem expresses the square-root bound in the existing extended-nonnegative transport API as \(\operatorname{projectedRMS}(\pi_N,P_\theta,\theta_*)\le\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}\).

KIPLMC/Dynamics.lean.title: Construct physical-time particle paths and derive their synchronous contraction
KIPLMC/Dynamics.lean.summary: The particle-average potential has the original pair curvature and smoothness constants, so the physical-time kinetic system can reuse the shared existence and nonlinear contraction theorems directly. The temperature changes the additive noise amplitude; the synchronous contraction does not depend on that amplitude because the common forcing cancels. The results here are explicit path statements, not stationary-law endpoints.

steps.title: Verify differentiability and smoothness of the average
steps.body: The lifted potential is differentiable whenever the pair potential is differentiable. Multiplying its value by the constant \(1/N\) preserves differentiability, yielding averagePotential_differentiable. The gradient has already been identified pointwise with the actual particle force. Function extensionality turns those equalities into equality of the vector fields, allowing averagePotential_gradient_lipschitz to rewrite the force's proved Lipschitz estimate as an estimate on the actual gradient. The result uses the original pair constant \(L\), independent of \(N\).

steps.title: Apply the kinetic integral-equation construction to the real particle force
steps.body: With \(N>0\), the force is globally Lipschitz. The shared kinetic existence theorem therefore constructs a continuous phase path satisfying \(Y_t-Y_0=-\int_0^tD_F(Y_s)ds+(B_t,0)\) on any finite nonnegative horizon, for every continuous velocity forcing starting at zero. The call uses inverse mass one because the force already equals \(\nabla\bar U_N\). Choosing physical-time Brownian amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\) gives the intended scaled particle forcing, but a complete probabilistic strong-solution result also identifies the driving Brownian law and independence conditions.

steps.title: The nonlinear contraction rate is independent of particle dimension
steps.body: Apply the shared potential contraction theorem to \(\bar U_N\). Its required hypotheses are derived by the average-potential differentiability, strong-convexity and smoothness theorems. Rewrite each gradient in the difference equation using \(\nabla\bar U_N=F\). With equal initial velocities, \(\gamma>0\), and \(\gamma^2\ge m+L\), the resulting bound is \(\|x_t-y_t\|\le\sqrt2e^{-mt/\gamma}\|x_0-y_0\|\). Neither \(N\) nor \(d_\theta+Nd_x\) appears in its rate. The theorem still explicitly requires continuous paths satisfying the noise-cancelled derivative equations; it does not replace construction of a stationary kinetic reference or taking the Wasserstein infimum.

KIPLMC/Laws.lean.title: Measurable transitions and actual iterated particle laws
KIPLMC/Laws.lean.summary: The pathwise algorithm maps become probability transitions by integrating them against independent fresh-noise measures. This module reuses the generic Markov-law construction and independence argument already proved for ULA. For KIPLMC1 it accepts a specified correlated phase innovation law; KIPLMC2 uses an explicit pair of independent standard Gaussian vectors for its two OU half steps. Law equality is kept distinct from convergence rates.

steps.title: Construct the OBABO noise law and prove both step maps measurable
steps.body: obaboNoise is the product of two standard Gaussian measures on the particle Euclidean space. Its product probability instance gives total mass one. Lipschitzness of the actual particle force implies continuity. Unfolding the exponential or OBABO map shows that each is built from this continuous force, coordinate projections, addition and scalar multiplication, so each uncurried state–noise map is continuous and hence measurable. Lean supplies force continuity first, applies Continuous.measurable, and discharges the finite composition with fun_prop.

steps.title: Define numerical laws by independent-noise pushforwards
steps.body: kiplmc1Laws applies the shared Markov recursion with the actual exponential step, an initial phase measure \(\mu\), and a supplied innovation measure \(\eta\). kiplmc2Laws uses the actual OBABO step and its fixed two-Gaussian noise measure. Each successor law is the pushforward of the product of the current-state law and the fresh-noise law. The probability theorems invoke the proved step measurability and probability of the initial and innovation measures, so every iterate is a genuine probability measure. For KIPLMC1 the covariance specification of \(\eta\) remains explicit and separate; probability alone does not identify the intended correlated Gaussian law.

steps.title: Prove the explicit exponential recursion has the Markov law
steps.body: First show that kiplmc1Chain equals the generic noise-driven recursion. Induction is exact: both start at the same phase and their successor expressions use the same step and innovation number. The law theorem then assumes a measurable initial random phase, a jointly independent innovation sequence with common law \(\eta\), and independence of initialization from the whole sequence. The shared generic result derives the law at every step; no additional per-step state–noise independence premise is inserted. Rewriting the explicit recursion by the proved equality yields the pushforward identity with kiplmc1Laws. This theorem establishes actual-law correspondence, while a quantitative sampling estimate still requires moment and coupling analysis for the specified Gaussian innovation.

steps.title: The independent-Gaussian OBABO trajectory has the constructed transition law
steps.body: kiplmc2Chain iterates the actual OBABO map with the two thermostat vectors from each supplied noise pair. If these pairs are independent across time, have the product-standard-Gaussian law obaboNoise, and are independent of initialization, then the pushforward of the pathwise recursion equals kiplmc2Laws at every step. The generic independence theorem derives independence of the current state from the fresh pair from these global assumptions. The proof is a direct reuse of that theorem with the established measurable OBABO map. Independence within each pair is encoded by its product Gaussian law; it is not confused with the independent sequence of pairs. This completes the actual algorithm-law correspondence, while contraction and the discrete invariant-measure bias remain separate quantitative obligations.

steps.title: Choose the constructed kinetic Gaussian for Algorithm 1
steps.body: The generic law identity accepts a specified iid innovation measure. kiplmc1GaussianLaws supplies the actual correlated Gaussian measure constructed in Noise.lean, whose spatial pairs have the shared kinetic Gram covariance. Thus the transition and its particle scaling are explicit. The earlier iid realization theorem specializes to this measure, with ordinary independence of initialization and fresh innovations. A convergence theorem must still derive a target comparison for these laws; the definition does not encode one.

KIPLMC/Rescaling.lean.title: Exact velocity and clock conjugacies
KIPLMC/Rescaling.lean.summary: The physical-time particle implementation can be expressed in unit-temperature kinetic coordinates by scaling velocity and the clock. This module proves the deterministic conjugacy of the actual exponential map and the damping identity. Gaussian covariance scaling and Brownian time-change laws remain distinct probabilistic results.

steps.title: Invert the velocity scale
steps.body: rescaleVelocity sends \((v,x)\) to \((cv,x)\). If \(c\ne0\), applying the inverse scale yields \((c^{-1}cv,x)=(v,x)\). Lean simplifies the nested scalar action and cancels the nonzero factor. Position is unchanged, so a parameter-position projection commutes with this part of the change of variables.

steps.title: Conjugate the shared exponential step
steps.body: The exact coefficient scaling gives \(\psi_{c\gamma,k}(h/c)=\psi_{\gamma,k}(h)/c^k\). Apply a step with force \(g\), friction \(c\gamma\), duration \(h/c\), initial velocity \(cv\), and additive innovation whose velocity component is also scaled by \(c\). Its result equals the velocity rescaling of a physical-time step with force \(g/c^2\), friction \(\gamma\), duration \(h\). Lean proves the two scalar cancellations for the first primitive, expands the map coordinatewise, rewrites all coefficient scales, and normalizes the resulting vector identities with module. The innovation here is already additive; obtaining its prescribed Gaussian law under this conjugacy requires a separate covariance computation.

steps.title: Check the invariant friction–step product and particle scale
steps.body: The OU damping depends on the product \(\gamma h\), so \(e^{-(c\gamma)(h/c)/2}=e^{-\gamma h/2}\) for \(c\ne0\). Lean unfolds the damping definition, reduces equality of exponentials to equality of exponents, and cancels the nonzero factor with field_simp. For the particle choice \(c=\sqrt N\), the coefficient identity \(((\sqrt N)^2)^{-1}=N^{-1}\) follows from the nonnegative square-root square theorem. Consequently the sum-potential force in rescaled time corresponds to the average-potential force in physical time.

KIPLMC.lean.title: Kinetic proof library and imports
KIPLMC.lean.summary: This root module imports the checked components of the kinetic development. Its dependencies contain the exact mathematical statements, assumptions and complete Lean proofs. An import collection does not by itself assert that every theorem in the source paper has been formalized; the source correspondence audit separately records the required full stochastic-law endpoints.

KIPLMC/Check.lean.title: Logical-axiom audit
KIPLMC/Check.lean.summary: This audit asks Lean to print the logical axioms used by selected declared results. It helps detect unproved assumptions masquerading as proofs. Passing an axiom audit checks the listed declarations; it does not establish source-paper completeness. The full required stochastic endpoints remain separately listed in the reference audit.

KIPLMC/Noise.lean.title: The actual correlated Gaussian particle innovation
KIPLMC/Noise.lean.summary: Velocity and position innovations within a coordinate share a Brownian source and are correlated. Distinct spatial coordinates are independent. This module constructs that joint probability measure using the kinetic library's two-dimensional Gram Gaussian, directly on the parameter-and-particle coordinate set. It works also when one of the dimensions is zero.

steps.title: Construct independent spatial Gaussian blocks and assemble phase vectors
steps.body: The coordinate set is \(I=\{1,\ldots,d_\theta\}\sqcup(\{1,\ldots,N\}\times\{1,\ldots,d_x\})\). For each \(i\in I\), take the shared kinetic Gaussian \((\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_i\prime)\sim\mathcal N(0,C_{\gamma,h})\), independently across \(i\). Their finite product measure is exponentialNoiseBlocks. The assembly map collects the first entries into the velocity vector and the second entries into the position vector. Lean defines these two Euclidean vectors with WithLp.toLp and proves the map measurable coordinate by coordinate. Pushing the product measure forward gives exponentialNoise. Probability follows from the Gaussian probability instances and preservation of total mass under the measurable map; no normalization assumption is supplied.

steps.title: Prove coordinate independence and retain the within-pair covariance
steps.body: The product-space evaluation maps are independent, so the Gaussian blocks belonging to distinct coordinates are independent. Evaluating the assembled velocity and position at a fixed spatial coordinate recovers its original two-dimensional Gaussian block exactly. Lean composes the two pushforwards, proves equality of the composed function with the block evaluation map by checking the two possible indices, and uses the product-measure evaluation law. The covariance of the pair is therefore exactly the kinetic Gram matrix, already proved positive semidefinite in the shared library. Multiplication by \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\) is performed by the particle step, not by this base noise law.

KIPLMC/FlowLaw.lean.title: Actual KIPLD position laws and particle-independent contraction
KIPLMC/FlowLaw.lean.summary: The scaled configuration space is \(\mathbb R^{d_\theta+Nd_x}\), with potential \(\bar U_N=V_N/N\). Its gradient is the actual physical-time particle force. The original pair potential's strong convexity and gradient Lipschitz constants pass to \(\bar U_N\) unchanged. Consequently the shared kinetic flow theorem applies with the original \(m,L,\gamma\), independently of the number of particles. This module constructs a probability law by an independent product and pushforward, and proves contraction of those actual laws. It does not assume Gibbs stationarity or identify an arbitrary forcing law with Brownian motion.

steps.title: Use the Borel structure of continuous forcing paths
steps.body: The velocity input lives in the compact-path space VelocityForcing T. Its natural measurable structure is its Borel structure. The two local instances install that structure and its defining compatibility witness. This makes the product of an initial velocity with a continuous forcing path an ordinary measurable source space. These are typeclass instances, not probabilistic independence hypotheses; independence will come from an explicit product measure.

steps.title: Construct the physical-time position law
steps.body:
For an initial position law \(\mu\) and a joint source law \(Q\) of velocity and continuous input, form \(\mu\otimes Q\). Evolve each pair with the selected kinetic integral flow for \(\nabla\bar U_N\) and project to its position at time \(t\). The resulting pushforward is kipldPositionLaw. Its definition calls the shared kineticPositionLaw, supplying the proved Lipschitz gradient of \(\bar U_N\). The normalization of the forcing subtracts its value at zero, so every continuous source path gives the correct initial condition. The Brownian specialization will choose the physical amplitude \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\); the definition deliberately admits any source law.

For \(0\le t\le T\), the endpoint is measurable because the selected flow depends continuously on its initial state and forcing. The product of probability inputs is a probability measure, and a measurable pushforward preserves total mass. kipldPositionLaw_probability invokes exactly this proved shared result.

steps.title: Transfer the true Wasserstein infimum without a new stochastic axiom
steps.body:
Let \(\mu, u\) have finite \(W_2\), and use the same source distribution \(Q\), independent of position for each evolution. If \(\gamma>0\) and \(\gamma^2\ge m+L\), then

\[W_2(P_t^Q\mu,P_t^Q u)\le\sqrt2e^{-mt/\gamma}W_2(\mu, u).\]

Lean applies the shared actual-law theorem to \( ar U_N\). The three analytic inputs are proved earlier: differentiability, strong convexity with parameter \(m\), and smoothness with constant \(L\). The theorem extends every initial coupling by the common independent source, proves its output marginals, bounds its cost using the actual integral-equation contraction, and takes the infimum. Thus the result concerns the actual pushforward laws. Finiteness of the output transport cost follows from the bound and the explicit finite initial-cost hypothesis before conversion from extended to real distance. To replace the second output by the Gibbs target requires the separate stationarity theorem; this statement does not hide that obligation.

KIPLMC/Moments.lean.title: Exact physical-temperature Gaussian velocity radius
KIPLMC/Moments.lean.summary: In scaled particle coordinates every velocity coordinate has variance \(1/N\). The thermal target is explicitly the image of a standard Gaussian under multiplication by \(N^{-1/2}\). This module proves the reverse normalization as an actual law equality and computes the exact L² radius \(\sqrt{(d_\theta+Nd_x)/N}\). No independence of coordinates is needed beyond what is already encoded by that Gaussian vector law; zero-dimensional spaces are included.

steps.title: Undo the thermal normalization as a pushforward equality
steps.body: For \(N>0\), the scalar \(\sqrt N\) is nonzero. Composing the target's defining map \(v\mapsto N^{-1/2}v\) with \(v\mapsto\sqrt Nv\) gives the identity on the configuration space. Lean rewrites the two successive pushforwards with Measure.map_map, proves the two scalar multiplications cancel using smul_smul and mul_inv_cancel₀, then applies Measure.map_id. Both maps are continuous and hence measurable. This is an exact distributional normalization, rather than a covariance-only assertion.

steps.title: Read off the L² moment from the actual Gaussian marginal
steps.body:
Suppose the L² random velocity \(V\) has the thermal marginal. The preceding map equality and HasLaw.comp show that \(\sqrt NV\) has the standard Gaussian law. The almost-everywhere scalar-multiplication rule for Lp representatives transfers this statement to the actual Lp class. The shared Gaussian-moment theorem therefore gives \(\|\sqrt NV\|_{L^2}=\sqrt{d_\theta+Nd_x}\). Since \(\sqrt N>0\), the norm scaling rule and division yield

\[\|V\|_{L^2}=\sqrt{\frac{d_\theta+Nd_x}{N}}.\]

Lean simplifies the cardinality of the sum/product coordinate index, rewrites the square root of a quotient, and divides by the strictly positive \(\sqrt N\). The moment is exactly the constant needed by the shared kinetic local-error argument at temperature \(1/N\).

KIPLMC/ReferenceBound.lean.title: The shared exponential proof at particle temperature
KIPLMC/ReferenceBound.lean.summary: The first particle algorithm uses exactly the shared exponential step. Its analytical comparison should therefore reuse the same proof. This module applies the shared L² kinetic theorem to the averaged lifted potential, uses the actual thermal Gaussian radius, and projects the resulting transport estimate to the MMLE parameter. The result has all three constants in the supplied KIPLMC1 theorem, with the initial supplied coupling cost. Its concrete integral-segment and reference-marginal hypotheses are explicit: construction of a canonical stationary reference and identification of the independent Gaussian chain are still needed for the unconditional sampler theorem.

steps.title: Lift the actual physical particle force once
steps.body: The averaged lifted potential \(\bar U_N=V_N/N\) has gradient \(F_N\), the physical-time force. The earlier geometry proves its original smoothness constant \(L\) and strong convexity constant \(m\), independently of particle count. lpForce applies the existing pointwise ULA.lpDrift construction to this gradient. It is therefore the actual particle force on almost-everywhere representatives, with a well-defined square-integrable output. No new exponential update or substitute gradient algorithm is introduced.

steps.title: Inherit the local comparison, recurrence, and sharp equilibrium term
steps.body:
Let \(S_n\) be numerical phase states and \(R_n\) reference phase states in L². On each interval, the auxiliary exact path starts at \(S_n\), the reference exact path starts at \(R_n\) and ends at \(R_{n+1}\), and their integral equations have the same additive input. The numerical endpoint is the actual shared exponential step with velocity noise \(B_h\) and position noise \(\int_0^hB_sds\). Its mild velocity and kinematic identities are explicit inputs. The reference velocity marginal is the thermal Gaussian and its position marginal is the normalized lifted Gibbs target.

The thermal moment theorem supplies \(C=\sqrt{(d_\theta+Nd_x)/N}\). Applying the shared kinetic theorem gives the full-state transport estimate with initial term \(\sqrt2(1-3mh/(4\gamma))^n\|S_0^X-R_0^X\|_{L^2}\) and bias \(Lh\sqrt2C/m\), under \(\gamma^2\ge m+L\) and \(4\gamma Lh\le m\). Every local-error and recurrence step is inherited, not assumed as a transport inequality.

The particular L² pair \((S_n^X,R_n^X)\) supplies a finite transport coupling, so real-valued conversion cannot conceal infinity. The parameter projection has operator norm at most one. The earlier sharp Gibbs concentration theorem contributes \(\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}\). Lean invokes the proved transport-to-projected-RMS triangle bound, proves the projected moment is finite, rewrites it as the square root of the actual parameter second moment, and adds the three terms. The resulting theorem remains explicitly a reference comparison; it does not assert that the unresolved reference construction has already been discharged.

KIPLMC/Contraction.lean.title: Contraction of the actual KIPLMC2 steps and chains
KIPLMC/Contraction.lean.summary: KIPLMC2 inherits the shared OBABO contraction by using the actual averaged particle potential. Its gradient is exactly the implemented particle force, and its strong convexity and smoothness constants remain \(m,L\), independent of the number of particles. The thermostat temperature changes the noise amplitude; common innovations cancel exactly in a synchronous comparison.

steps.title: Transfer the proved one-step phase inequality
steps.body: Write \(\mathcal E(v,x)=\lVert x\rVert^2+2\langle x,v\rangle/\gamma+\lVert v\rVert^2/L\). Under \(\gamma^2\ge4L\) and \(33\gamma^3h\le m\), the shared theorem proves \(\mathcal E(S(z,\xi,\xi\prime)-S(w,\xi,\xi\prime))\le(1-mh/(3\gamma))\mathcal E(z-w)\). Lean supplies the proved differentiability, strong convexity and Lipschitz gradient of the average potential, then rewrites its gradient as the actual force. Both thermostat inputs are the same in the two copies. No Gaussian assumption is needed for this pathwise inequality.

steps.title: Use the implemented chain recurrence at every step
steps.body: The chain is the concrete noise-driven recursion, not a sequence assumed to satisfy an estimate. Its successor identity supplies exactly the shared OBABO iteration hypotheses. Repeated contraction gives \(\mathcal E(Z_n-\widetilde Z_n)\le q^n\mathcal E(Z_0-\widetilde Z_0)\), where \(q=1-mh/(3\gamma)\). All noise values may be arbitrary: the result therefore applies to the Gaussian algorithm after its independent-noise law is constructed.

steps.title: Project to positions with a common initial velocity
steps.body: The phase energy satisfies \(\mathcal E(v,x)\ge\lVert x\rVert^2/2\). If the initial velocities agree, its initial value is exactly the squared initial position discrepancy. Taking square roots gives \(\lVert X_n-\widetilde X_n\rVert\le\sqrt{2q^n}\lVert X_0-\widetilde X_0\rVert\). The physical-time contraction does not acquire an artificial particle factor. This is the stability part of the sampling analysis; comparison with the Gibbs target also needs the separately proved discretization bias.

KIPLMC/OBABORescaling.lean.title: Exact unit-temperature transfer of the actual KIPLMC2 law
KIPLMC/OBABORescaling.lean.summary: Put \(c=\sqrt N\). Multiply the scaled physical velocity by \(c\), keep position unchanged, replace the clock step by \(h/c\), and replace friction by \(c\gamma\). The averaged force then becomes the gradient of the sum potential. Every subflow, the whole implemented trajectory, its independent Gaussian Markov law and its Gibbs target satisfy this exact change of variables. This is the probability-level bridge needed to reuse the shared OBABO sampling theorem.

steps.title: Check thermostat, drift and kick under the clock change
steps.body: The thermostat sends \(v\) to \(\delta v+\sigma\xi\); multiplying velocity by \(c\) changes its noise amplitude to \(c\sigma\). The drift satisfies \((h/c)(cv)=hv\), so position is unchanged. For the kick, \((h/c)g=c h(c^{-2}g)\). Lean proves each identity by unfolding the actual map, distributing scalar multiplication and cancelling the nonzero clock factor. Combining these equalities in their original O–B–A–B–O order proves the full five-subflow conjugacy, including both distinct fresh innovations.

steps.title: Keep the contracting metric exactly invariant
steps.body: The transformed potential has smoothness \(c^2L\) and friction \(c\gamma\). In its phase energy, the velocity term is \(\lVert cv\rVert^2/(c^2L)=\lVert v\rVert^2/L\), and the mixed term is \(2\langle x,cv\rangle/(c\gamma)=2\langle x,v\rangle/\gamma\). The position term is unchanged. Thus the entire weighted energy is invariant. Lean expands its definition, applies the norm and inner-product scalar rules, and cancels the positive \(c\).

steps.title: Identify the implemented particle step and entire trajectory
steps.body: Take \(c=\sqrt N\). The force \(N^{-1}\nabla V_N\) is precisely \(c^{-2}\nabla V_N\), damping depends only on \(\gamma h\), and \(\sqrt N\sqrt{(1-\delta^2)/N}=\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\). These established identities specialize the generic conjugacy to Algorithm 2. Induction through its concrete successor recurrence proves the entire transformed trajectory is the standard-temperature OBABO trajectory for \(V_N\), driven by exactly the same paired Gaussian vectors.

steps.title: Transport the actual Gibbs target and Markov laws
steps.body: The unit-temperature phase target is \(\mathcal N(0,I)\otimes\pi_{V_N}\). Multiplying its velocity by \(N^{-1/2}\) gives exactly the defined KIPLMC thermal target; position remains \(\pi_{V_N}\). The product pushforward identity proves this equality after strong convexity supplies probability normalization. For numerical laws, the proved step conjugacy and joint measurability feed the general Markov-law conjugacy theorem. It establishes the equality for the implemented independent-Gaussian law at every iteration, so transferring a sampling estimate requires no assumed correspondence between two algorithms.

KIPLMC/ExponentialRescaling.lean.title: Exact KIPLMC1 clock change for correlated Gaussian innovations
KIPLMC/ExponentialRescaling.lean.summary: The same positions and a velocity multiplication by √N convert physical-time KIPLMC1 into the shared unit-temperature exponential integrator for the sum potential. This file proves the actual covariance, Gaussian measure, update, initialization, and complete iterated-law identities. Both correlated noise components and their mutual covariance are transported explicitly.

steps.title: The Brownian clock changes each correlated block diagonally
steps.body: Write \(c>0\), \(\gamma^\prime=c\gamma\), and \(h^\prime=h/c\). A time change contributes a Brownian factor \(c^{-1/2}\); the position response contributes another factor \(c^{-1}\). The resulting map on the two-component Gaussian block is \[D_c(v,x)=(c^{-1/2}v,c^{-3/2}x).\] Lean constructs this diagonal map as an actual continuous linear map on Euclidean two-space. The coordinate theorem verifies the factors directly. The kernel accessor theorem identifies the two entries of the algorithmic kernel vector with \(\psi_0\) and \(\psi_1\), so the subsequent proof can use the already checked arbitrary-index response scaling.

steps.title: Prove the covariance transformation and the Gaussian measure identity
steps.body:
The covariance is the actual Gram integral \(C_{ij}(\gamma,h)=\int_0^h\psi_i(\gamma,t)\psi_j(\gamma,t)\,dt\), with \(i,j\in\{0,1\}\). The exact response identity \(\psi_i(c\gamma,t)=c^{-i}\psi_i(\gamma,ct)\), followed by the substitution \(s=ct\), gives \[C_{ij}(c\gamma,h/c)=c^{-(i+j+1)}C_{ij}(\gamma,h).\] These are precisely the entries of \(D_c C D_c^\mathsf T\), including the off-diagonal velocity-position covariance. Lean rewrites both response factors, moves their constants outside the integral, performs the checked interval-integral change of variables, and reduces the four finite index cases using \((\sqrt c)^2=c\).

Both measures are actual centered Gaussian measures. The mean of their linear pushforward is zero by commutation of the Bochner integral with the continuous linear map. Their covariance bilinear forms agree on the standard orthonormal basis by the displayed Gram identity, so Gaussian uniqueness proves \[(D_c)_\#\mathcal G_{\gamma,h}=\mathcal G_{c\gamma,h/c}.\] No Gaussian covariance or distributional scaling is introduced as a premise.

steps.title: Transport the independent spatial blocks without losing correlation
steps.body: The particle noise measure is the finite product of these two-component Gaussian blocks over the parameter and latent coordinate set. Lean applies the proved scalar Gaussian pushforward to each independent block, uses the exact product-measure mapping identity, and checks that assembling blocks into velocity and position vectors commutes with \(D_c\). Thus the full actual particle innovation obeys the same clock law. Independence between distinct spatial blocks is retained, while each block retains its exact velocity-position correlation.

steps.title: Conjugate the actual exponential update
steps.body: For \(c=\sqrt N\), multiply velocity by \(c\) and leave position fixed. Under the changed clock, the force becomes \(\nabla V_N\), the friction is \(c\gamma\), and the step is \(h/c\). The exact deterministic exponential response conjugacy has already been proved. What remains is the actual additive innovation: \[\sqrt{2c\gamma}\,D_c\xi=\bigl(c\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\,\xi_v,\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\,\xi_x\bigr).\] Lean proves these two scalar identities from the positive square roots and the checked particle amplitude identity, then rewrites the shared exponential map. The resulting equality is an identity of the implemented updates for every phase state and every supplied correlated innovation.

steps.title: Pass the clock identity through the actual Markov laws
steps.body: The generic innovation-mapping lemma proves that replacing the noise law by \(R_\#Q\) is exactly substituting \(R\xi\) in each transition. Its proof is an induction on the true iterated Markov measure: at each step, the product law is pushed through \((z,\xi)\mapsto(z,R\xi)\), then through the measurable update. The phase conjugacy theorem applies this fact together with the proved update identity and the exact Gaussian block scaling. Consequently the entire actual KIPLMC1 Gaussian Markov law, pushed through \((v,x)\mapsto(\sqrt N v,x)\), is exactly the shared unit-temperature KLMC Markov law for \(V_N\) at \((\sqrt N\gamma,h/\sqrt N)\). The equality includes the noise measure and every iteration, rather than merely comparing update formulas.

steps.title: Identify the thermal initialization and the unchanged position marginal
steps.body: The physical velocity target is the explicit Gaussian pushforward \(N^{-1/2}\mathcal N(0,I)\). Multiplication by \(\sqrt N\) returns the actual standard Gaussian law. Since the position is left fixed, the independent thermal initialization becomes \(\mathcal N(0,I)\otimes\nu\) for every initial position law \(\nu\). Lean proves this using the actual product-measure pushforward and the already checked thermal velocity normalization. Finally, applying the position projection to the full iterated-law identity proves that the actual KIPLMC1 position law equals the unit-temperature KLMC position law at the changed clock. This supplies the exact law transfer needed to import the shared kinetic error estimate without duplicating its analysis.

KIPLMC/CanonicalExponential.lean.title: KIPLMC1: the unconditional parameter RMS bound for the actual Gaussian sampler
KIPLMC/CanonicalExponential.lean.summary: The actual KIPLMC1 Gaussian Markov laws are identified with the shared canonical KLMC laws at the changed clock. The shared kinetic theorem constructs its Brownian reference, proves exact Gibbs stationarity, controls the real local error, and takes the true coupling infimum. The particle geometry and sharp parameter concentration then give the paper’s three explicit error terms.

steps.title: Identify the actual particle noise source with the actual Gaussian Markov law
steps.body: The particle coordinate set is \(\mathrm{Fin}(d_\theta)\sqcup(\mathrm{Fin}(N)\times\mathrm{Fin}(d_x))\). The shared kinetic construction now works directly on this arbitrary finite set. Its complete canonical innovation stream has the proved product law of independent spatial blocks, each with the exact correlated two-component Gaussian distribution. Lean instantiates the checked product-source Markov-law theorem with this actual Brownian source, its actual whole-stream law, and an independent standard Gaussian initial velocity. This identifies the concrete canonical kinetic position law with the position marginal of the actual Gaussian Markov iterate. The previously checked particle clock theorem then gives the exact identity between the physical-time KIPLMC1 output and this same canonical output for \(V_N\) at friction \(\sqrt N\gamma\) and step \(h/\sqrt N\). The position target is unchanged.

steps.title: Check the transformed assumptions and all particle-count cancellations
steps.body: In scaled particle coordinates, the sum potential \(V_N\) has strong convexity \(Nm\) and gradient Lipschitz constant \(NL\). Put \(c=\sqrt N\), \(\gamma^\prime=c\gamma\), and \(h^\prime=h/c\). The original restrictions \(m+L\le\gamma^2\) and \(4\gamma Lh\le m\) become exactly \[Nm+NL\le(\gamma^\prime)^2,\qquad4\gamma^\prime(NL)h^\prime\le Nm.\] Lean proves positivity, curvature compatibility, friction, and step conditions together using \(c^2=N\), then proves the exact rate identity \[1-\frac{3(Nm)h^\prime}{4\gamma^\prime}=1-\frac{3mh}{4\gamma}.\] For \(D=d_\theta+Nd_x\), the shared bias simplifies exactly to \[\frac{NLh^\prime\sqrt{2D}}{Nm}=\frac{Lh}{m}\sqrt{\frac{2D}{N}}.\] The scalar proof checks the square-root quotient with nonnegative dimensions and the positive particle count. This cancellation explains why the first algorithm’s error contains \(d_x+d_\theta/N\), with no additional growing power of particle count.

steps.title: Derive finite transport moments for the actual output
steps.body: The initial position law has the stated finite second moment. Strong convexity proves the corresponding moment of the actual normalized Gibbs target; their independent product therefore supplies a finite transport coupling. The shared canonical construction places this coupling on the same genuine Gaussian/Brownian source as the actual chain. Its numerical and exact reference positions are actual L² random variables, and exact reference stationarity has already been proved from the splitting limit. Their actual L² discrepancy supplies a finite output transport coupling. Lean transfers this finiteness through the exact particle law identity. Thus the later real-valued Wasserstein and parameter RMS expressions are used only after their finiteness has been proved.

steps.title: Apply the shared kinetic theorem to the actual particle sampler
steps.body: The shared theorem is applied to the genuine sum potential, using its derived \(Nm\)-strong convexity and \(NL\)-smoothness. It proves, rather than assumes, the stationary Brownian reference, source independence, mild identities, local exponential-integrator error, scalar recurrence, and transport infimum. Lean supplies the transformed assumptions proved above, rewrites the actual output through the exact clock/Gaussian-law identity, counts the finite particle coordinates, and simplifies the rate and bias. The resulting actual position-law estimate is \[W_2(\nu_n,\pi_N)\le\sqrt2\left(1-\frac{3mh}{4\gamma}\right)^nW_2(\nu,\pi_N)+\frac{Lh\sqrt2}{m}\sqrt{\frac{d_\theta+Nd_x}{N}}.\] The initialization in this theorem is explicitly the independent thermal velocity law times the supplied position law; all algorithmic Gaussian correlations are those of the constructed noise measure.

steps.title: Project to the parameter and add the sharp equilibrium concentration
steps.body: The parameter projection is a continuous linear map with norm at most one. The actual powered Gibbs parameter marginal satisfies the proved sharp concentration bound \(\mathbb E_{\pi_N}\|\theta-\theta_\star\|^2\le d_\theta/(Nm)\). The checked transport-to-RMS inequality therefore gives \[\bigl(\mathbb E\|\theta_n-\theta_\star\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le\sqrt2\left(1-\frac{3mh}{4\gamma}\right)^nW_2(\nu,\pi_N)+\frac{Lh\sqrt2}{m}\sqrt{\frac{d_\theta+Nd_x}{N}}+\sqrt{\frac{d_\theta}{Nm}}.\] Lean invokes the actual output finiteness theorem, the sharp equilibrium concentration theorem, and the nonexpansive projection theorem. It rewrites the finite RMS as the displayed square root of the Bochner integral and substitutes the proved actual Gaussian position-law estimate. These are the initialization, discretization, and finite-particle concentration errors in the paper’s theorem.

steps.title: Recover the paper’s independent-initialization constant
steps.body: The true initial Wasserstein distance is bounded by every actual initial coupling cost. In particular, independent \(Z_0\sim\nu\) and \(\bar Z_\star\sim\pi_N\) give \[W_2(\nu,\pi_N)\le\bigl(\mathbb E\|Z_0-\bar Z_\star\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.\] Lean constructs this independent product coupling, derives the integrability of its discrepancy from the two proved second moments, and rewrites its finite L² cost as the actual square-root integral. It also proves that the stated step restrictions make the geometric rate nonnegative. Multiplying the initial coupling inequality by this nonnegative rate gives exactly the paper’s printed constant \(C_1\); the other two constants are unchanged. Thus the true-transport statement and the printed independent-initialization statement are both checked consequences for the same actual sampler.

KIPLMC/OBABOBound.lean.title: The actual KIPLMC2 sampling and parameter RMS bounds
KIPLMC/OBABOBound.lean.summary: The entire KIPLMC2 error estimate follows from the actual shared OBABO sampler, its exact particle clock change and the sharp parameter concentration theorem. Every initial law, Gaussian innovation, target transport and finite output moment is established internally. The explicit bound below has the intensive dimension \(\sqrt{(d_\theta+Nd_x)/N}\), and consequently also implies the supplied manuscript’s coarser particle dependence.

steps.title: Transfer the independent thermal initialization and actual position law
steps.body: The physical scaled velocity law is \(N^{-1/2}\) times a standard Gaussian, independently of the initial position \(\nu\). Multiplication by \(\sqrt N\) restores the exact independent standard-Gaussian initialization. The product pushforward identity proves this equality. Applying the already proved whole-chain Markov conjugacy and then projecting to positions gives equality of the actual KIPLMC2 position law and the standard-temperature OBABO position law at \(\gamma\prime=\sqrt N\gamma\), \(h\prime=h/\sqrt N\), for the actual sum potential \(V_N\).

steps.title: Cancel all clock factors in rate and admissibility
steps.body: With a general positive clock factor \(c\), curvature becomes \(c^2m,c^2L\), friction becomes \(c\gamma\), and the step becomes \(h/c\). Hence \(m\prime h\prime/(3\gamma\prime)=mh/(3\gamma)\). The friction threshold \(4L\le\gamma^2\) and the step threshold \(33\gamma^3h\le m\) are preserved by multiplying through by \(c^2\). Lean proves these cancellations directly, keeping the nonzero clock factor explicit.

steps.title: Recover the intensive particle bias
steps.body:
The shared OBABO position bias is \(6\sqrt2\gamma\prime h\prime\sqrt{d_z}(4\sqrt{L\prime}+L\prime h\prime/2)/m\prime\). Substitute the exact clock and curvature values. Since \(\sqrt{c^2L}=c\sqrt L\), cancellation gives

\[\frac{6\sqrt2\gamma}{m}h\sqrt{\frac{d_z}{N}}\left(4\sqrt L+\frac{Lh}{2}\right),\qquad d_z=d_\theta+Nd_x.\]

The algebraic theorem records the exact equality of the two expressions, not just an asymptotic comparison.

steps.title: Apply the genuine OBABO sampling theorem
steps.body:
The sum potential inherits strong convexity \(Nm\) and smoothness \(NL\) from the original joint potential. Its Gibbs target is exactly the defined lifted particle target. The theorem applies the proved unit-temperature sampler bound, transports its actual position law through the exact conjugacy, and simplifies the rate and bias. It proves both finiteness of the output Wasserstein distance and

\[W_2(\nu_n,\pi_N)\le\sqrt2\left(1-\frac{mh}{3\gamma}\right)^{n/2}W_2(\nu,\pi_N)+\frac{6\sqrt2\gamma}{m}h\sqrt{\frac{d_z}{N}}\left(4\sqrt L+\frac{Lh}{2}\right).\]

The actual two-thermostat Gaussian laws are part of the constructed Markov recursion. No stationarity, reference-path or local-error estimate is assumed.

steps.title: Project to the parameter and add the sharp concentration term
steps.body: The initial finite second moment and strong convexity give a finite initial transport distance. The preceding theorem gives finite output transport. The parameter projection has norm at most one, so its RMS error around the unique MMLE is bounded by the position transport distance plus the Gibbs parameter RMS error. The latter is at most \(\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}\). The final theorem therefore adds this third term to the actual KIPLMC2 sampling estimate and expresses the result as the genuine square root of the parameter-error integral.

KIPLMC/OBABOPaperRate.lean.title: The supplied KIPLMC2 rate with an explicit dimension-independent constant
KIPLMC/OBABOPaperRate.lean.summary: The preceding actual sampler theorem gives a stronger intensive bias. This module derives the precise coarser form printed in the supplied manuscript, including its additional transient term. The implicit constant is replaced by an explicit expression that depends only on \(m,L,\gamma\), and the final result concerns the actual parameter-error integral.

steps.title: Turn the square-root geometric factor into the printed exponential
steps.body: Let \(r=\sqrt{1-mh/(3\gamma)}\). The scalar bound \(1-x\le e^{-x}\), followed by taking square roots, gives \(r\le e^{-mh/(6\gamma)}\). Raising to the actual integer iteration index proves \(r^n\le e^{-mhn/(6\gamma)}\). The proof also handles a nonpositive square-root argument directly, so the scalar envelope itself does not need an extra admissibility hypothesis.

steps.title: Make the hidden constant explicit
steps.body:
The allowed step satisfies \(h\le m/(33\gamma^3)\). Consequently the physical bias coefficient is bounded by

\[B=\frac{6\sqrt2\gamma}{m}\left(4\sqrt L+\frac{Lm}{66\gamma^3}\right).\]

Choose \(C=\sqrt2+B+1/\sqrt m\). All three summands are nonnegative, so \(C\) dominates the transient coefficient, bias coefficient and equilibrium concentration coefficient separately. Lean proves these comparisons from positivity, without permitting dependence on the particle count, dimensions or step.

steps.title: Compare each term with the supplied coarse particle envelope
steps.body: For \(N\ge1\), \(D\le\sqrt N D+hN\sqrt{d_z}\) and \(\sqrt{d_z/N}\le\sqrt{Nd_z}\). The equilibrium term satisfies \(\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}=(1/\sqrt m)\sqrt{d_\theta/N}\). Apply the exponential rate envelope, dominate each coefficient by \(C\), and add the three inequalities. This proves the exact printed shape, including the harmless nonnegative extra transient contribution \(hN\sqrt{d_z}\), from the sharper estimate.

steps.title: Apply the envelope to the actual particle parameter law
steps.body:
The final theorem starts from the unconditional actual KIPLMC2 RMS estimate and supplies every scalar hypothesis using the original curvature, friction and step restrictions. With \(D=W_2(\nu,\pi_N)\), it proves

\[\sqrt{\mathbb E\lVert\theta_n-\theta_\star\rVert^2}\le C\left[(\sqrt ND+hN\sqrt{d_z})e^{-mhn/(6\gamma)}+h\sqrt{Nd_z}+\sqrt{d_\theta/N}\right].\]

This is the supplied manuscript theorem with an explicit constant and the actual independent Gaussian algorithm law. The proof does not assume its desired RMS estimate as an input.

KIPLMC/KineticClock.lean.title: The exact physical-time integral equation
KIPLMC/KineticClock.lean.summary: Let \(Y_s\) solve the unit-temperature kinetic equation with sum force \(g\) and friction \(c\gamma\). The physical process is \(S_t=D_{c^{-1}}Y_{t/c}\), where \(D_a(v,x)=(av,x)\). This module proves the complete transformed integral equation in any complete normed vector space, including the L² space of actual random variables used by the Brownian construction.

steps.title: Make velocity scaling a bounded linear map
steps.body: The velocity projection multiplied by \(c\), paired with the unchanged position projection, defines a continuous linear map. Its action is exactly rescaleVelocity. Linearity allows this map to pass through Bochner integrals; continuity ensures the transformed path remains continuous. Expanding the phase drift proves \(c^{-1}D_{c^{-1}}R_{g,c\gamma}(z)=R_{c^{-2}g,\gamma}(D_{c^{-1}}z)\). The two powers of \(c^{-1}\) in the force come from time and velocity separately.

steps.title: Change variables inside the actual integral equation
steps.body: For \(0\le t\le T\), positivity of \(c\) gives \(t/c\in[0,T/c]\). Apply the continuous linear map to the given solution identity at \(t/c\), pass it through the integral, and substitute \(r=s/c\). The drift identity identifies the transformed force and friction, and the additive source becomes \(c^{-1}B_{t/c}\). Lean proves equality of the complete vector-valued integrals, not merely equality of formal differential symbols. This theorem requires no derivative of the Brownian input.

KIPLMC/Continuous.lean.title: The actual Brownian KIPLD flow and its stationary mixing theorem
KIPLMC/Continuous.lean.summary: This module connects the canonical Brownian kinetic diffusion to the physical particle system and proves Proposition 3 for its actual output law. The initial position is an arbitrary probability law with finite second moment. Standard Gaussian velocity and the canonical Brownian source are independent of that position; velocity scaling gives the required physical thermal law. The Gibbs law is a proved stationary target, and the Wasserstein distance is the infimum over all couplings.

steps.title: Construct the source, the physical flow, and its actual endpoint law
steps.body: Set \(c=\sqrt N\). The canonical source contains a standard Gaussian velocity and an independent vector Brownian source on the actual coordinate set \(\mathrm{Fin}(d_\theta)\sqcup(\mathrm{Fin}(N)\times\mathrm{Fin}(d_x))\). Use the proved selected kinetic flow with sum potential \(V_N\), smoothness \(NL\), and friction \(c\gamma\). The physical process is \(D_{c^{-1}}Y_{t/c}\). Position is unchanged, so its endpoint pushforward is exactly the canonical position law at time \(T/c\). This exact equality is the bridge used by the convergence proof.

steps.title: Verify the independent thermal initialization
steps.body: The complete source law theorem supplies the actual initial phase law \(\mathcal N(0,I)\otimes\nu\). Push it through velocity multiplication by \(N^{-1/2}\). The result is precisely velocityTarget.prod ν; the velocity and position remain independent. The selected flow’s time-zero identity and the almost-everywhere scalar-multiplication rule identify the actual L² representatives with this pushforward. No initialization-law hypothesis is imposed on the final theorem.

steps.title: Cancel the clock factors and prove stationary mixing
steps.body: The lifted potential has curvature \(Nm\) and smoothness \(NL\). Multiplication by \(N\) transforms \(m+L\le\gamma^2\) into \(Nm+NL\le(\sqrt N\gamma)^2\), so the actual canonical Gibbs mixing theorem applies. Its exponent is \(-(Nm)/(\sqrt N\gamma)\,(T/\sqrt N)=-mT/\gamma\). The resulting estimate is \(W_2(\nu_T,\pi_Z)\le\sqrt2e^{-mT/\gamma}W_2(\nu,\pi_Z)\). The canonical theorem proves Gibbs stationarity internally. Separate moment and probability theorems certify that all real Wasserstein quantities are finite.

steps.title: Identify the actual physical force in the integral equation
steps.body: The drift lifted to L² represents pointwise application of the true sum gradient. The almost-everywhere scalar multiplication and composition identities show that \(N^{-1}\operatorname{lpDrift}(\nabla V_N)=\operatorname{lpDrift}(F)\), where \(F=\nabla V_N/N\) is the previously verified particle force. Apply the exact kinetic clock theorem to the selected canonical solution. The result is the full physical-time integral equation with friction \(\gamma\), the actual force \(F\), and input \(N^{-1/2}B_{t/\sqrt N}\). The shared Brownian scaling theorem identifies its thermal amplitude as \(\sqrt{2\gamma/N}\).

steps.title: Project to the parameter and add the statistical error
steps.body: The parameter projection has operator norm at most one, so pushing any coupling through it cannot increase its quadratic cost. Taking the true coupling infimum bounds the parameter Wasserstein distance by the full position distance. The initial independent coupling \(\nu\otimes\pi_Z\) bounds that infimum by \((\mathbb E\|Z_0-\bar Z_*\|^2)^{1/2}\), giving precisely the printed proposition. A second endpoint adds the already proved sharp equilibrium concentration radius \(\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}\) by the L² triangle inequality, giving a direct parameter RMS bound about the unique marginal-likelihood maximizer.

KIPLMC/Accuracy.lean.title: Explicit particle, step, and iteration accuracy budgets
KIPLMC/Accuracy.lean.summary: These corollaries turn both actual particle-sampler theorems into finite epsilon guarantees. Statistical concentration, discretization, and initialization receive separate budgets. Integer ceilings and positive minimum steps make the prescriptions valid without informal asymptotic rounding.

steps.title: Control KIPLMC1 with three concrete budgets
steps.body: Write its actual bound as \(\sqrt2(1-\alpha)^nD+b+s\). Allocate \(b,s\le\varepsilon/3\), and choose the checked logarithmic count so the geometric factor times \(D\) is at most \(\varepsilon/24\). These fit within the shared \(0.94\varepsilon\) persistent-error allocation. The algorithm theorem supplies the bound internally, with its actual Gaussian law and MMLE target. Only choices of \(N,h,n\) remain in the hypotheses. Since \(b=(\sqrt2 L/m)h\sqrt{d_\theta/N+d_x}\) and \(s=\sqrt{d_\theta/(Nm)}\), the formula exposes the first method’s dimension and accuracy dependence directly.

steps.title: Round the exponential and statistical requirements
steps.body: The exponential budget uses \(n\ge\lceil\max\{0,\log(24D/\varepsilon)/\alpha\}\rceil\), with a separate zero-\(D\) case. Monotonicity of the exponential and \(e^{-\log x}=x^{-1}\) give \(De^{-\alpha n}\le\varepsilon/24\). For a square-root statistical floor \(C\sqrt{d/N}\), choose \(N=\max\{1,\lceil9C^2d/\varepsilon^2\rceil\}\). The ceiling inequality, multiplication through \(N>0\), and the square-root identity prove the floor is at most \(\varepsilon/3\). Zero parameter dimension is included.

steps.title: Choose the step and inspect the dimension algebra
steps.body: For a positive stability cap \(A\) and positive linear-bias coefficient \(B\), the explicit choice \(h=\min\{A,\varepsilon/(3B)\}\) is positive, respects stability, and has \(hB\le\varepsilon/3\). This applies to each method’s displayed bias. The exact source identity \(\sqrt{N(d_\theta+Nd_x)}=(d_\theta/\varepsilon)\sqrt{1+d_x/\varepsilon^2}\) at the idealized choice \(N=d_\theta/\varepsilon^2\) explains the supplied KIPLMC2 complexity. Integer ceilings affect constants and are handled by the previous theorem. Lean proves the identity by equality of nonnegative squares.

steps.title: Apply the supplied KIPLMC2 rate with its uniform constant
steps.body: Let \(C\) be the explicit constant depending only on curvature and friction, and set \(A=\sqrt N D_0+hN\sqrt{d_z}\). Apply the rounded exponential budget to \(D=CA\), with \(\alpha=mh/(6\gamma)\). Allocate \(Ch\sqrt{Nd_z}\le\varepsilon/3\) and \(C\sqrt{d_\theta/N}\le\varepsilon/3\). The actual Gaussian-chain theorem then gives RMS error at most \(\varepsilon\). For fixed curvature constants, the particle choice has order \(d_\theta/\varepsilon^2\), the small-error step has order \(\varepsilon^3/(d_\theta\sqrt{d_x})\), and the displayed reciprocal-step logarithmic threshold yields the source’s iteration order. Polynomial growth of initial distance is the additional condition under which that logarithm is suppressed in the source’s tilde notation.

KIPLMC/Stationarity.lean.title: Full physical KIPLD Gibbs stationarity
KIPLMC/Stationarity.lean.summary: The invariant density calculation is certified as an actual flow-law theorem: the complete physical Brownian phase process, started at its normalized Gaussian-times-Gibbs target, has that same target distribution at every nonnegative time.

steps.title: Transport the proved full phase stationarity through the exact clock
steps.body: The canonical selected flow for the sum potential preserves \(\mathcal N(0,I)\otimes\pi_Z\), by the shared kinetic stationarity theorem. Push this actual endpoint law through \(D_{1/\sqrt N}(v,z)=(v/\sqrt N,z)\). The product pushforward is exactly \(\mathcal N(0,N^{-1}I)\otimes\pi_Z\), namely gibbsPhaseTarget. The physical KIPLD flow was defined by this very time and velocity change. Lean’s almost-everywhere scalar-multiplication identity identifies its L² phase representative with the pushed canonical representative. This proves invariance of the whole phase law, including velocity–position independence, rather than only the position marginal or a formal zero-generator calculation.

KIPLMC/LogisticExample.lean.title: Logistic regression: actual gradient, Hessian, and convexity scope
KIPLMC/LogisticExample.lean.summary: The Bayesian logistic example has a Gaussian location prior and finitely many Bernoulli observations. The formal model is \(U(\theta,x)=\frac{\tau}{2}\|x-\theta\|^2+\sum_j[\log(1+e^{\langle v_j,x\rangle})-y_j\langle v_j,x\rangle]\), where \(\tau=\sigma^{-2}\). Additive normalization constants do not affect any derivative. This chapter derives the actual joint gradient and its Fréchet derivative, proves the exact global smoothness constant printed in the paper, and proves convexity and the full-span strict-convexity statement. It also proves that no finite unregularized model in a nonzero latent dimension has a positive global strong-convexity constant. Consequently the experimental model illustrates the algorithms but does not automatically satisfy the hypotheses of the quantitative convergence theorems.

steps.title: Differentiate a single observation
steps.body: For a single response, write \(\ell_y(u)=\log(1+e^u)-yu\). The logarithm is evaluated at a positive argument, so the ordinary chain rule gives \(\ell_y'(u)=e^u/(1+e^u)-y=s(u)-y\). Lean first identifies Mathlib's sigmoid with this exponential ratio, then composes the exponential and logarithm derivative rules. The curvature is \(q(u)=s(u)(1-s(u))\). Since \(0<s(u)<1\), it is positive. The identity \(q(u)=1/4-(s(u)-1/2)^2\) gives \(q(u)\le1/4\). The mean-value theorem therefore supplies a global \(1/4\)-Lipschitz theorem for the sigmoid. These arguments do not require the response to be binary; the source's Bernoulli choices are included.

steps.title: Derive the first and second variations from the model
steps.body: Take any affine joint line \((\theta,x)+t(u,w)\). The prior contributes \(\tau\langle x-\theta+t(w-u),w-u\rangle\) to the score. Observation \(j\) contributes \([s(\langle v_j,x+tw\rangle)-y_j]\langle v_j,w\rangle\). Differentiating this actual scalar function again gives \(\tau\|w-u\|^2+\sum_jq(\langle v_j,x+tw\rangle)\langle v_j,w\rangle^2\). The Lean proof constructs the derivative of each affine coordinate, applies the squared-norm rule and the single-observation rule, and adds the finitely many derivatives. The second proof differentiates the resulting score. Thus the displayed quadratic form is justified by calculus on the original potential.

steps.title: Find the exact Hessian nullspace
steps.body: Every term in the second variation is nonnegative when \(\tau\ge0\). If \(\tau>0\), a zero total forces \(w-u=0\) and \(\langle v_j,w\rangle=0\) for every feature. Conversely those equations make every term vanish. Lean isolates the nonnegative prior term, bounds each observation term by the whole sum, and uses strict positivity of every logistic weight to cancel it. If the features span the latent space, orthogonality to every feature extends to their linear span by submodule induction. Taking the inner product with \(w\) itself then gives \(w=0\), and hence \(u=0\). Every nonzero joint direction therefore has strictly positive second variation at each finite state.

steps.title: Prove global convexity and full-span strict convexity
steps.body: To compare two joint states \(z,z'\), restrict the actual potential to \(F(t)=U(z+t(z'-z))\). The two derivative theorems identify \(F''\) with the nonnegative quadratic form. The real-variable second-derivative criterion proves convexity of \(F\). Applying its Jensen inequality at \(t=0,1\) yields the full joint convexity inequality. Under the span assumption and \(z\ne z'\), the direction is nonzero, so the second derivative is positive at every finite \(t\). The strict second-derivative criterion yields strict Jensen inequality. Lean explicitly rewrites \(z+b(z'-z)=az+bz'\) using \(a+b=1\), so the conclusion concerns the original joint potential on the whole space.

steps.title: Use the Euclidean norm for the actual joint gradient
steps.body: The source norm is the Euclidean product norm \(\|(\theta,x)\|^2=\|\theta\|^2+\|x\|^2\). Mathlib's ordinary product has a maximum norm, so the formalization uses WithLp 2 (E × E) for these gradient claims. The coordinate equivalence is continuous and linear. Differentiating the prior and all finite observations proves Fréchet differentiability. The explicit gradient is \((-\tau(x-\theta),\;\tau(x-\theta)+\sum_j[s(\langle v_j,x\rangle)-y_j]v_j)\). To identify it with the actual Hilbert gradient, Lean compares the Fréchet derivative applied to an arbitrary direction with the already proved directional score, expands the product inner product, and uses uniqueness of derivatives. The resulting equality is with the library's gradient, not a separately named surrogate force.

steps.title: Recover the exact printed global smoothness constant
steps.body: The prior block maps a joint difference \((a,b)\) to \((a-b,b-a)\). Its squared norm is \(2\|b-a\|^2\le4(\|a\|^2+\|b\|^2)\), hence its operator norm is at most two. For observation \(j\), the sigmoid Lipschitz bound and Cauchy–Schwarz give \(\|(s(\langle v_j,x\rangle)-s(\langle v_j,x'\rangle))v_j\|\le\frac14\|v_j\|^2\|x-x'\|\). The latent coordinate projection has norm at most one. Adding these bounds proves \(\|\nabla U(z)-\nabla U(z')\|\le(2\tau+\frac14\sum_j\|v_j\|^2)\|z-z'\|\). The Lean proof first certifies the squared-norm estimate, then bounds each summand, and finally decomposes the actual gradient difference into its prior and observation parts. With \(\tau=\sigma^{-2}\), this is exactly the source constant.

steps.title: Identify the full block Hessian as a genuine Fréchet derivative
steps.body: The operator is \(\nabla^2U(\theta,x)=\tau\begin{pmatrix}I&-I\\-I&I\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\sum_jq(\langle v_j,x\rangle)v_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}\). Each rank-one observation block sends a direction \((u,w)\) to \((0,q_j\langle v_j,w\rangle v_j)\). Lean constructs these maps as continuous linear maps, forms their finite sum, and transports the block operator to the Euclidean joint space. Differentiating both actual gradient coordinates with the Fréchet chain rule gives exactly this operator. Expanding its product inner product recovers the earlier curvature formula. This closes the connection between the matrix printed in the experiment and the derivative used by the formal calculus.

steps.title: An explicit full-rank counterexample separates strict from strong convexity
steps.body: Already one scalar feature \(v_1=1\) spans the latent space. With response one and common location \(\theta=x=t\), the Gaussian prior vanishes and \(U(t,t)=\log(1+e^{-t})\). For \(t\ge0\), this lies between zero and \(\log2\). A positive strong-convexity constant \(m\) would force the midpoint inequality between \((0,0)\) and \((2t,2t)\) to contain the negative correction \(-mt^2\). Choosing \(t^2=(\log2+1)/m\) makes that right-hand side negative, contradicting nonnegativity. Lean proves the logarithm identity, both bounds, the exact Euclidean distance, and this contradiction. The full-span theorem applies to this example, so strict convexity is compatible with failure of every positive uniform lower curvature bound.

steps.title: Prove the strong-convexity caveat for every finite unregularized model
steps.body: The obstruction is general. For every real response and predictor, \(\ell_y(u)\le\log2+(1+|y|)|u|\), because \(1+e^u\le2e^{|u|}\). Along any nonzero common translation \((\theta,x)=(tw,tw)\), the prior stays zero, while the finitely many observation terms grow at most linearly: \(U(tw,tw)\le|J|\log2+|t|C_w\), where \(C_w=\sum_j(1+|y_j|)|\langle v_j,w\rangle|\). Applying a hypothetical strong-convexity midpoint inequality to the opposite states at \(\pm t\) forces \(m\|w\|^2t^2\le C_wt\). Choose \(t=(C_w+1)/(m\|w\|^2)>0\) to contradict it. This proves the source caveat in every nonzero latent dimension, regardless of feature rank. It explains why further regularization is needed before applying the paper's global strong-convexity convergence bounds to these experiments.
